clue.text: Posh decoration by novice, this flower cluster

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A snob's medal is pinned beside a beginner's, next to a spray of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists use the term for a flat-topped spray of small blooms on stalks from one point, as in cow parsley.

clue.text: Was she in front of house when it fell?

definitions.text: Was she in front of house when it fell?

parts.words: Was she in front of house when it fell?
parts.note: a cinema attendant works front of house; the fall also recalls Poe's tale The Fall of the House of Usher, with a feminine ending

explanation.surface: A question about a theatre worker's whereabouts when the building collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' reads as a theatre, but it also points to Poe's story The Fall of the House of Usher; add the feminine -ETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who shows patrons to their seats in a cinema or theatre works front of house.

clue.text: Do dancers prop it up? Quite the reverse

definitions.text: Do dancers prop it up? Quite the reverse

parts.words: Do dancers prop it up? Quite the reverse
parts.note: ballet dancers lean on a fixed rail for support while practising, so it holds them up rather than they holding it

explanation.surface: A question about whether dancers hold something up, answered with a reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' is not a reversal signal here: it means the rail props the dancers up.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet practice rail fixed to the studio wall supports dancers during exercises.

clue.text: Has ample time to see lurid version

indicators.note: a new version of the words gives a rearranged form of their letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with time on their hands can read a sensational edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well supplied with free hours, not tied by work, is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Found one passage to censure

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gate is a passage or opening through a wall

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a corridor and uses it to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to rebuke or criticise severely.

clue.text: Wall-eyed saint?

definitions.meaning: Mr ..., the British wartime graffiti figure, peers with big eyes over a wall

explanation.surface: A question about a holy man with a squint.
explanation.walkthrough: MR CHAD was a doodle of a bald face peering over a wall, captioned 'Wot no ...?', common in Britain from the 1940s.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the wall-peeping cartoon face and to an Anglo-Saxon bishop of Lichfield.

clue.text: Candle maker, said to be from Wales

definitions.text: Candle maker, said to be from Wales

parts.words: Candle maker, said to be from Wales
parts.note: a waxy substance once used for candles comes from the head of a sperm whale, and 'whales' sounds like 'Wales'

explanation.surface: A chandler who supposedly hails from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wales' is spoken for 'whales': the wax is taken from the sperm whale.
explanation.definitionFit: This waxy oil from the whale's head was prized for making fine candles.

clue.text: Peri with no love left for this Cretan girl

indicators.note: the Peri is to be without the two letters that follow, so they come out

parts.note: Iolanthe is the fairy (peri) of Gilbert and Sullivan's opera, subtitled The Peer and the Peri
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A fairy with no love remaining for a young woman from Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peri' looks like a name, but it is the fairy Iolanthe from Gilbert and Sullivan; take O and L out.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ovid's Metamorphoses a girl of Crete is betrothed to Iphis.

clue.text: This conveyance is invalid — look at the crosses on it

definitions.text: This conveyance is invalid — look at the crosses on it

parts.words: This conveyance is invalid — look at the crosses on it
parts.note: a vehicle carrying invalids, marked with red crosses

explanation.surface: A deed of transfer is void because of the crosses marked on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conveyance' and 'invalid' sound legal (a void deed); read them as a vehicle for the sick, painted with red crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency vehicle that carries the sick and injured often bears a red cross.

clue.text: Board the coach by the motorway, we're told

indicators.note: the phrase signals the words are heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: a coach on the motorway is an M bus, M being the British motorway label

explanation.surface: Getting on the coach beside the motorway, as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: British motorways are lettered M (M1, M25), so a motorway bus is an 'M bus'.
explanation.definitionFit: To get aboard a vehicle, especially of troops onto transport, is the sense here.

clue.text: Wine from the Leningrad collection?

definitions.meaning: a Rhone red from the hill of that name
the great art museum of St Petersburg, called Leningrad in Soviet times

explanation.surface: A bottle from a Russian museum's holdings.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a northern Rhone appellation and the famous St Petersburg museum.

clue.text: Catch the old boy — he made a fortune in India

definitions.text: he made a fortune in India

parts.note: to nab is to catch
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Arresting a former pupil who got rich in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The word was used for Europeans who came home wealthy from service in the Raj.

clue.text: Sort of look you get from a literary don

parts.words: you get from a literary don
parts.note: Don Quixote is called the Knight of the Sorrowful Countenance, a woeful face

explanation.surface: A kind of expression a university lecturer might give.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' suggests a university lecturer; it is Don Quixote, 'the Knight of the ___ Countenance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A regretful, sorrowful expression is described by this adjective.

clue.text: No representative has look in — the boss is here!

parts.note: O, a zero, means none
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

indicators.note: look is placed inside the word has

parts.note: taken as written
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: A complaint that no MP has looked in while the chief is present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is not a chief but a raised centre, as on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word means a navel or central knob, the boss of a shield, or the world's centre at Delphi.

clue.text: Below par on the greens it's disconcerting!

parts.note: feeling below par is feeling off
golfers putt on the greens

explanation.surface: A golfer finds poor putting unsettling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean unsettling or repellent.

clue.text: Start working to seize power

parts.note: to take is to seize
effect is force or power to produce a result

explanation.surface: Beginning a job by grabbing control.
explanation.definitionFit: When a law or drug begins operating it comes into force.

clue.text: Lines cut off by Porlock businessman

definitions.text: Lines cut off by Porlock businessman

parts.words: Lines cut off by Porlock businessman
parts.note: Coleridge said his poem was broken off when a person from Porlock called on business

explanation.surface: A trader from a Somerset village interrupts a recital.
explanation.walkthrough: Porlock is a village in Somerset, England; Coleridge's unfinished poem about Xanadu is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's dream poem was left unfinished after a visitor from Porlock interrupted him.

clue.text: Protuberance in the back row

indicators.note: read backwards, the word for row is taken from the back

parts.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers or taxis

explanation.surface: A lump found in the rear row.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a knot or knob on a tree trunk, a bump.

clue.text: Rising again. River Ure gets name for turbulence

indicators.note: the letters are churned about as in rough water

parts.note: taken as written; the Ure is a Yorkshire river
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire river gains a reputation for rough water as it rises again.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something recovering and coming back to strength.

clue.text: Vehicle worth a pile to the dramatist

parts.note: a rick is a stack or pile of hay
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A vehicle worth a fortune to a playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled cart pulled by a person is a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Live on the Spanish river

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece sits on, next after, the other

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: Living beside a river in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A major German waterway flowing to the North Sea at Hamburg.

clue.text: It's spent so badly it's an irregularity

indicators.note: the words are put together badly, out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wasting money like that is improper.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchiness or unevenness, being blotchy, is a kind of unevenness.

clue.text: School that stirs up clods

definitions.meaning: a famous English public school in north-west London
a frame of spikes dragged over ploughed land to break up soil

explanation.surface: An establishment that churns up lumps of earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a celebrated English boarding school and a farm implement for breaking soil.

clue.text: Intolerable acts followed one such social gathering

definitions.text: Intolerable acts followed one such social gathering

parts.words: Intolerable acts followed one such social gathering
parts.note: Britain passed the Intolerable Acts in 1774 after Boston colonists dumped tea in the harbour

explanation.surface: Unbearable behaviour after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intolerable acts' looks like bad behaviour; it is the name of the British laws punishing Boston after its 1773 protest.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon get-together with cups and cakes, and the Boston protest of 1773.

clue.text: Signal for a lift — one of those that go up or down

definitions.meaning: a hitch-hiker raises a digit to ask for a ride

definitions.text: one of those that go up or down
definitions.meaning: a digit turned up or down gives approval or rejection

explanation.surface: A gesture asking for a ride, or one used in a lift going up or down.
explanation.definitionFit: The short digit is used for hitch-hiking and for the up or down verdict.

clue.text: He won't work, but within limits can ski very well

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the bounds of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A slacker who can nonetheless ski well within bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a shirker who avoids work or school.

clue.text: Little weight would be attached to this composer's judgement

indicators.note: the small weight must be attached to the composer to give the judgement, so here it comes off

parts.note: a verdict is a judgement
CT is the abbreviation for carat, a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A composer's opinion carries little weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Composer plus CT (carat) would make VERDICT, a judgement; the clue works backwards from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe, the Italian author of Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Continue to fool

explanation.surface: Keep acting the idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: As two words, a phrase meaning proceed; as one, slang for a clown.

clue.text: Consumer admits husband is the master

indicators.note: lets in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a user is one who consumes

explanation.surface: A shopper lets her husband in; he's the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly an assistant schoolteacher was so called, a junior schoolmaster.

clue.text: Old puffer reverses order of the Cavalry Club

indicators.note: the two pieces are given in the opposite order in the clue, so they swap

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
horse means mounted troops, cavalry

explanation.surface: An old smoker reshuffles the membership of a military club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavalry Club' looks like the name of a London gentlemen's club; read its two words separately, and 'reverses order of' makes them swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: A nineteenth-century nickname for a steam locomotive.

clue.text: BA changes gown and gets jumped on by supporters

parts.note: taken as written; a Bachelor of Arts

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A graduate swaps gowns and gets mobbed by fans.
explanation.walkthrough: To jump on the bandwagon is to join a popular cause.
explanation.definitionFit: People join a fashionable cause by climbing aboard it, in the idiom.

clue.text: About which some girls used to be waspish

definitions.text: About which some girls used to be waspish

parts.words: About which some girls used to be waspish
parts.note: Victorian corsets gave women narrow middles like a wasp's

explanation.surface: Some girls were once snappish on a topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waspish' looks like irritable; it means wasp-like in shape, the narrow middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The narrow part of the body between ribs and hips was tightly corseted.
